# Hive

> Hive is a portable guidance layer for deliberate work with coding agents. It supplies shared rules, activity skills, and specialist role definitions, plus a Go manager that installs them into the native locations of Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Pi, OpenCode V2, Cursor CLI, and Antigravity. Each host keeps its own model loop, authentication, tools, permissions, and history. Building the manager from source requires Go 1.27.4 or later.

Distributable content lives in `content/` and `integrations/`; the manager is in `tooling/`. `_support/`, `tests/`, and the root `AGENTS.md` are maintainer material for this repository and are not installed; `site/` is the documentation site for people and is not installed either. Links are relative to the repository root.

## Docs

- [Documentation site](https://hive.tricell.tech/): getting started, a skills catalog with flow guides, a flows overview, inspiration projects, and a changelog rendered from CHANGELOG.md; each flow page links to its skill
- [README](README.md): overview, installation (one-line, release package, or source), hosts, update, recovery, and uninstall. One-line install: `curl -fsSL https://hive.tricell.tech/install.sh | sh`; append `-s -- --dry-run --hosts <hosts>` to preview without changing any host, which needs no terminal; a real installation needs a terminal. `hive update` installs a compatible published release (0.9.0 or newer), after installations of 0.8.0 or earlier run the 0.9.0-or-newer installer once; `hive update --source DIR` remains the committed-source route
- [One-line installer script](get-hive.sh): what the one-line command downloads and runs
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): release history, starting with 0.1.0
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): local test suite, viewer frontend development (Node >=24 and pnpm 12.8.1), checked-in bundle freshness, conventions, and language rules
- [Security](SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability privately
- [Installer contract](_support/docs/architecture/installer.md): package checks, migration, and interrupted-install recovery
- [Deployment manager](_support/docs/architecture/deployment-manager.md): manager commands, plans, scopes, ownership, and recovery
- `hive voice list|set|off`: list the voices, select one, or turn it off (see the manager contract above)
- `hive project set`: edit the `## Hive` section of a repository's `AGENTS.md` after confirmation; the section holds facts, and `hive doctor` exits non-zero on a blocking finding in it
- `hive releases`: list the retained release snapshots
- `hive time`: print, as JSON, an agent session's active time, its waits for the user and on remote CI, and the time converted for a ticket's worklog
- [Agent delivery](_support/docs/architecture/agent-delivery.md): canonical roles, native profiles, and per-host delegation limits

## Guidance

The global core retains essential boundaries and explicit read conditions for
canonical procedures. Reporting is read under the conditions
`content/guidance/global.md` states, not before every reply; other procedures
are selected by their stated conditions, not all preloaded. A packaged
file, its discovery, its delivery into context and compliance are separate facts.
Source-byte unions are not actual tokens or evidence of small-model reliability.

- [Shared guidance](content/guidance/global.md): the invariants every session needs (authorization, preservation, secrets, artifact placement, delivery modes, persistent memory, one invariant line for questions and routes) and the index of the rule leaves that hold the rest, grouped by domain, installed into each host
- [hive-mode ticket-status playbook](content/skills/hive-mode/playbooks/ticket-status.md): report the backlog and unfinished work, read-only, and recommend what to take next
- [Rule leaves](content/guidance/global.md): the «Rule leaves» section of the global guidance indexes the leaves stored in the hidden `hive-core` skill (`content/skills/hive-core/<domain>/<name>.md`, one folder per domain listed in `content/skills/hive-core/assets/domains.json`), each one rule read as a file at the moment its line names, never invoked as a skill; `hive-core` sets `disable-model-invocation: true` (Claude Code reads it; the manager generates `agents/openai.yaml` for Codex; Antigravity lists the skill; no mechanism is verified for the other hosts)
- [Code principles](content/skills/hive-core/principles/index.md): hidden index of the principles in `content/skills/hive-core/principles/`, each read at the moment its line names; it links `hive-typescript` (`content/skills/hive-typescript/SKILL.md`), the one model-invocable leaf; its `paths` field limits when Claude Code and Cursor list it, other hosts ignore the field, and on every host the agent reads it by choice, not automatically
- [hive-mode](content/skills/hive-mode/SKILL.md): entry router for every request to do work: settle what the user needs and pick one of 13 playbooks (`playbooks/<kind>.md`) by the kind of work, then answer, continue into build, or go to plan only when the how has a decision for the user; also investigates a question, assesses a chosen ticket or audits a codebase for what to improve, ending analyses at the findings
- [create-design](content/skills/create-design/SKILL.md): design work in four entries. Draw (optional stage between research and plan): draw one example of a new or recomposed screen as frames in the project's Figma file, following the app's existing screens (alternatives only for a screen the user names), have the completed set reviewed, then ask once to approve or correct it, with applicable mobile frames ready, and record the approved examples the plan, build and verification compare against, with a rule card beside each frame for its business rules, which the work also writes to its ticket when the example is approved, when the build starts and at the close; corrections return only affected screens for approval, while proposed business rules remain separate decisions; a web app is drawn at its desktop width plus 440 px when served on mobile, a mobile-only app once at 440 px, and a yes to recording the Figma file or library in `DESIGN.md` stays pending for the plan to write. Correct: change the frames a request names. Review: one `hive-review-ux` child reviews a design someone else drew, given as a Figma link or an image, and returns findings, missing states, unsettled rules as questions and a verdict, drawing nothing. Create or refresh `DESIGN.md`: detect the project's component library, installed version and customization layer, keep them in a verified `DESIGN.md`, and give design, build and review work measurable UI criteria below the project's own design system (`content/skills/create-design/references/ui-criteria.md`)
- [flow-plan](content/skills/flow-plan/SKILL.md): settle the how: present approaches, resolve decisions and define contracts, tasks, and acceptance criteria
- [flow-build](content/skills/flow-build/SKILL.md): implement authorized work and hand over a built candidate
- [flow-verify](content/skills/flow-verify/SKILL.md): verify the candidate with the checks its kind always gets, a code review on every non-mechanical change and a security review recommended for a change to a security boundary, then integrate it
- [flow-close](content/skills/flow-close/SKILL.md): move the ticket, write the work's business rules to it and report at integration, end as the close's situation sets (the footer of replies, or the report alone), and clean up the work's resources, the evidence its ticket or merged pull request holds, and the merged branches and clean worktrees of each repository it touched before the report, leaving for a close reply only what needs the user, record the change folder's archive for a hygiene batch that archives every pending folder in one delivery, commit the change folder at a pause where the specs repository allows it, honoring a `Completion` key's later completion point
- [flow-deploy](content/skills/flow-deploy/SKILL.md): promote an integrated candidate through the declared environments and verify what is served, moving tickets to the final state a `Completion` key names
- [create-issue](content/skills/create-issue/SKILL.md): create a tracker ticket, break work down into a parent ticket with children, or validate an existing ticket, so a person or an agent can work it without inventing decisions; used when the user asks for a ticket or answers that a finding becomes one
- [create-prd](content/skills/create-prd/SKILL.md): write a requirement document in PRD format for a module or feature, restructure one that someone else wrote, update it with its author's answers, or review it against the code, so development builds from rules it does not have to decide; used when the user asks for a requirement document or a PRD
- [git-workflow](content/skills/git-workflow/SKILL.md): prepare authorized Git delivery while preserving unrelated work
- [flow-verify walkthrough](content/skills/hive-core/ui/walkthrough.md): publish UI captures and their iteration to the viewer, and present a built interface for validation
- [create-report](content/skills/create-report/SKILL.md): a designed HTML report, comparison, explainer or deck
- [create-report docs-site mode](content/skills/create-report/references/docs-site.md): scaffold, extend or audit a documentation site
- [harness-audit](content/skills/harness-audit/SKILL.md): audit agent instructions, skills and role definitions, ask the decisions the findings need, and apply the accepted outcomes, including a repository's `## Hive` section and its `## Skills` registry, checked with skill_registry.py
- [harness-audit local instructions mode](content/skills/harness-audit/references/local-instructions.md): create or prune the untracked HIVE.local.md of a project and the machine file (~/.config/hive/HIVE.local.md) from what already worked on this machine, after asking which facts to keep
- [harness-audit personal rules mode](content/skills/harness-audit/references/personal-rules.md): write the user's own rules once in ~/.config/hive/rules.md, after the user approves the text, and copy them with personal_rules.py to every host where Hive is installed; check or remove the copies
- [hive-mode dependency-security playbook](content/skills/hive-mode/playbooks/dependency-security.md): check whether a published advisory affects a set of repositories, without changing them
- [comment-audit](content/skills/comment-audit/SKILL.md): audit a codebase's comments in batches, file a ticket for each excuse, move each recorded decision to the project's decision record, add a lint that rejects new comments, and generate the project's own skill to repeat it
- [test-audit](content/skills/test-audit/SKILL.md): prune one area's duplicate or implementation-coupled tests to one owner per contract, proven by an independent review and targeted mutations
- [project-layout](content/skills/project-layout/SKILL.md): hold a project's layout convention (where docs, scripts and data go, the project index), check a project against it, and clean up, reorganize or migrate it through a manifest you confirm, in a repository, workspace or monorepo, with or without Hive
- [workspace-repo](content/skills/workspace-repo/SKILL.md): turn a workspace of several repositories into a coordinator repository that versions its guidance and knowledge, only when you ask
- [unattended-delegation](content/skills/unattended-delegation/SKILL.md): coordinate delegated work with a bounded objective and expiry
- [harness-audit Engram workspace mode](content/skills/harness-audit/references/engram-workspace.md): establish one Engram identity for a declared workspace, only when asked
- [Role profiles](integrations/agent-profiles.json): default model and effort per role and host
- [Instruction resources](_support/docs/architecture/instruction-resources.md): canonical procedure homes, resolution, payload validation and declared reading-footprint scenarios
- [Optional OpenCode context loader](_support/docs/architecture/deployment-manager.md#optional-opencode-context-loader): delivered inactive at user scope as `<OpenCodeHome>/hive/context-loader/{index.js,context-loader.json}`, outside `plugins/`, with no `package.json`; activate only the installed `hive/context-loader` directory, not the editorial template. It supplies two fixed-role snapshots without runtime reference/metadata reads; refresh requires manager regeneration and plugin reload, not a live Markdown edit. Metadata schema 2 records role/resource/digest provenance, not cryptographic authentication. Deactivation/removal preserves user configuration. Package manifest v2 is separate from metadata schema 2; v1 packages remain readable by the current manager

## Optional

- [Local viewer](README.md#review-ui-walkthroughs-in-one-place): shared-work timeline of UI captures with their iteration, immutable evidence and current canonical references; agents publish only captures with `hive view work capture`, while stage, task, evidence and Markdown publication stay as advanced operations (`hive view work contract`, `hive view contract`); the browser's management actions also from the CLI (`hive view work rename|archive|restore|pin|unpin|recover|delete`); automatic visibility archival after closure, manual content retention, capture publication (`work capture`, closed with `work close`, queued while the viewer is stopped), host-observed session activity and native tasks through `hive hook` registered per host at user-scope install (Codex needs approval in `/hooks`), and a coordinated timeline revision 3 update within protocol 3
- [Viewer manual](site/src/content/docs/viewer.md): read tasks, stage activity, galleries, document revisions, canonical references and CI waits; manage the local work library.
- [Viewer frontend](tooling/viewer/frontend/README.md): standalone development package, real API by default, explicit development preview, same-tab navigation persistence, bundle contract and checks
- [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): Go and embedded frontend license notices

- [Repository structure](_support/docs/architecture/repository-and-distribution.md): layout, ownership, and managed instruction blocks
- [Optional tool dependencies](_support/docs/architecture/tool-dependencies.md): Engram, Context7, pi-subagents (whose `extensions/subagent/config.json` gets `"toolActivation": "eager"` when the key is missing, with `hive plan remove`), agent-browser, the Codex question card (`codex-question-card`, subject to the host's question and mode restrictions), the Codex wait floor (`codex-wait-floor`, which writes `min_wait_timeout_ms` and `default_wait_timeout_ms` under `[features.multi_agent_v2]` in Codex's `config.toml`, with a backup and `hive plan remove`), and CodeGraph
- [Harness engineering research](_support/docs/harness-engineering/README.md): research sources and the measurement standard
- [Model support floor](_support/docs/harness-engineering/model-floor.md): the models the guidance is written for (role-profile models) and the floor candidates, Haiku, flash-class and the maintainer's main-session models included, whose observed failures count toward a correction
- [History and provenance](_support/docs/history/history-and-provenance.md): how the project evolved
- [Requirements and change records](_support/openspec/): versioned requirements and planned changes
- [Tests](tests/): content checks, fixtures, and evaluation tooling
